summary: The @gyomu/config package provides a centralized mechanism for managing, merging, and resolving hierarchical application settings. It leverages functional programming principles to coordinate configuration retrieval across global, user, and scoped sources, ensuring that consumers receive validated and strongly-typed data.
responsibilities: Orchestrate the multi-stage resolution of configuration values from diverse sources.
Enforce precedence and merging logic to generate a coherent application state.
Validate resolved configuration against defined schemas before providing it to the application.
Provide structured error reporting and contextual metadata to support fault-tolerant configuration lookups.
Maintain lifecycle awareness of the configuration resolution process.

capabilities.name: Configuration Resolution Service
capabilities.description: Provides a primary interface for querying and obtaining application settings based on specific resolution criteria.

capabilities.name: Hierarchical Merging
capabilities.description: Automates the aggregation of configuration data across different scopes, ensuring consistent precedence between global, user, and functional contexts.

capabilities.name: Fault-Tolerant Resolution
capabilities.description: Offers rich error context and lifecycle tracking to allow consumers to handle resolution failures and determine retriability.

designDecisions: Utilizes the Effect ecosystem to represent configuration retrieval as a manageable effect, supporting composability and dependency injection.
Employs a query-based resolution pattern to separate configuration retrieval criteria from the underlying data sources.
Standardizes configuration errors by grouping them within a lifecycle-aware context to improve debuggability and system reliability.
usageGuidance: Inject the ConfigResolver service into application layers to safely access validated configurations.
Define resolution queries precisely to avoid unnecessary overhead and ensure correct scope application.
Handle potential configuration resolution errors using the provided context, specifically checking for retryable status when appropriate.
